envelope.text: /// zero is "not reported", never "published at time zero".

why:
both sides carry per-message metadata. SHIPPED 2026-10-25 (issue 2036): `rclcpp::MessageInfo` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/message_info.hpp`) exists and is what a hosted `(msg, const rclcpp::MessageInfo&)` subscription callback receives, in all four message forms. `get_rmw_message_info()` is upstream's accessor, both constnesses.

THE DIVERGENCE, and its constraint: upstream's accessor returns `rmw_message_info_t`; ours returns `rclcpp::RmwMessageInfo`, the same members under the same names (`source_timestamp`, `received_timestamp`, `publication_sequence_number`, `reception_sequence_number`, `publisher_gid.data[24]`, `from_intra_process`), because the C++ surface does not include the RMW ABI headers that define the C type. Member access reads the same; a declaration spelled `rmw_message_info_t` is a COMPILE ERROR. `publisher_gid.implementation_identifier` is null (one RMW per session) and `from_intra_process` is always false.

POPULATION is a backend property: the values come from the backend's `take_with_info` (Rust `nros::MessageInfo`, see `rust:MessageInfo`); a field a backend does not report is zero, so zero means "not reported": uORB reports nothing, XRCE only `received_timestamp` (issue 2135), Cyclone everything but `received_timestamp`. A freestanding build refuses the callback shape at compile time (`NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_MESSAGE_INFO_CALLBACK`): the metadata path keeps the callable on the heap. The POLLING take with metadata, `PollSubscription<M>::take(M&, MessageInfo&)` (issue 2074), needs no heap and is offered on freestanding builds too.

Test: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/subscription_message_info_runtime.cpp` (stub backend, all four shapes, `just check cpp`).
